extracted.intended_audience: general readers, fans and researchers interested in the television series American Dad!
extracted.subtask_description: An encyclopedic/wikipedia-style overview of the animated TV series American Dad!, covering production history, episode/season counts and discrepancies, broadcast history, ratings, critical reception, awards, home media and related media. The page is informational rather than a how-to or guideline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Writing in an Animated Television Production (Annie Awards)
rubrics_metrics.description: Annie Award category for writing in an animated TV production (page lists Dan Vebber nominated for "The American Dad After School Special" in 2007).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implicitly treats script/writing quality as an evaluative dimension worthy of award recognition; used as evidence of writing excellence when nominated or won.

rubrics_metrics.name: Directing in a Television Production (Annie Awards)
rubrics_metrics.description: Annie Award category recognizing directing in television animation (page lists Pam Cooke and Jansen Lee nominated in 2010 for "Brains, Brains & Automobiles").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Positions directorial craft in animation as a criterion for critical recognition and evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Animation TV Programming (Artios Awards)
rubrics_metrics.description: Artios Award category referencing animation television programming (page shows nominations in this category).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Casting/production and programming-level quality can be an awards-based criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Television Animation (Artios Awards listings)
rubrics_metrics.description: Artios Award nomination entries labeled 'Television Animation' across multiple years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broadly denotes industry recognition of animation-specific production standards for TV shows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Top Television Series (ASCAP Awards)
rubrics_metrics.description: ASCAP award category recognizing top television series (American Dad! won in 2013).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Musical/score-related industry recognition can serve as a metric for overall series quality in awards contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outstanding Individual Episode (GLAAD Media Award)
rubrics_metrics.description: GLAAD category for an outstanding single episode (page lists nomination for "Lincoln Lover").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Single-episode thematic or social-issue excellence is evaluated independently from series as a whole.

rubrics_metrics.name: Animated Series (Gold Derby Awards)
rubrics_metrics.description: Gold Derby Awards category recognizing an animated series (page lists nominations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Overall series quality in animation (storytelling, production, comedy) measured at the series level.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Sound Editing in Television Animated (Golden Reel Awards)
rubrics_metrics.description: Golden Reel Award category for sound editing in animated television (multiple nominations listed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical sound-editing quality in animation is an explicit evaluative dimension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Favourite International TV Show (It List Awards)
rubrics_metrics.description: It List Awards category acknowledging an international favorite show (page lists a nomination).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: International popularity/favorability functions as an evaluative metric separate from domestic awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Favorite Animated TV Show (People's Choice Awards)
rubrics_metrics.description: People's Choice Awards category reflecting popular-vote evaluation of animated TV shows (nominations listed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Audience/popularity-based awards measure viewer preference as a criterion of success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outstanding Animated Program (Primetime Emmy Awards)
rubrics_metrics.description: Primetime Emmy category for outstanding animated program (American Dad! nominated in multiple years).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prestige award measuring overall excellence in animated programming (writing, production, voice performance, direction).

rubrics_metrics.name: Outstanding Character Voice-Over Performance (Primetime Emmy Awards)
rubrics_metrics.description: Primetime Emmy category honoring individual voice performance (page lists nominations for voice actors).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Voice acting quality is a discrete evaluative dimension for animation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prism Award — Mental Health
rubrics_metrics.description: Prism Award recognizing portrayals related to mental health (American Dad! listed as winner in 2007).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accurate/meaningful portrayals of mental health topics can be recognized and are an evaluative dimension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prism Award — Comedy Episode
rubrics_metrics.description: Prism Award nomination category recognizing comedic episodes addressing relevant issues (nominated in 2009).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluates how comedic episodes handle socially relevant or health-related subject matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice Summer Series / Choice V-Cast / Choice TV: Animated Show (Teen Choice Awards)
rubrics_metrics.description: Teen Choice Awards categories (Choice Summer Series, Choice V-Cast, Choice TV: Animated Show) where the show has been nominated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Youth/audience-driven awards that reflect popularity and appeal among teen viewers as evaluation signals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience size and Nielsen ratings
rubrics_metrics.description: Season- and episode-level viewership metrics: premiere viewers, finale viewers, season rank, average viewers in millions (detailed season-by-season table).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quantitative audience metrics (Nielsen ratings, premiere/finale viewers, season averages) are used to evaluate commercial success and relative popularity across seasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Streaming-hours milestone (Disney+ / platform streaming metrics)
rubrics_metrics.description: Streaming-based popularity metric (page reports American Dad among series to surpass one billion hours streamed on Disney+ in 2025).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Modern success and reach are measured by total hours streamed on platforms; used as evidence of continued relevance/popularity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social-media popularity and geographic distribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Social-media metrics (e.g., Facebook Likes) and geographic popularity patterns (NYT study finding regional popularity in Northeastern, Mid-Atlantic and Great Lakes regions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Social engagement and geographic distribution of likes/viewer interest are used to characterize popularity and audience demographics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critical reception and topical engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Qualitative critical evaluation (Common Sense Media: the show addresses 'patriotism, generational divide, political activism, and traditional gender roles' with 'more fantasy than reality, but enough of the latter to touch a nerve with some grown-ups').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critical appraisal can focus on how well comedy engages social/political issues and balances fantasy with realism to resonate with adult audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Episode/season numbering and reporting accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Accuracy and consistency of episode/season numbering across networks and streaming services (multiple conflicting numbering models, misreporting of milestone episodes e.g., 150th vs 151st).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Correct episode sequencing and transparent numbering matters for archival, broadcast, and scholarly use; misreporting is highlighted as a problem and can confuse evaluations that rely on episode counts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Production quality differences (pilot vs series)
rubrics_metrics.description: Differences between the unaired precursory pilot and the series premiere in pictorial technique, coloration, character design and voice actors (pilot rougher/simpler drawings; Steve different design and voice).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Production polish, character design consistency, and voice casting are production-level criteria that affect perceived quality between pilot and series.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character development and use of recurring devices
rubrics_metrics.description: Characterization choices (e.g., Roger's running gag of alternate disguises and freedom to exist outside the house; multiple redesigns of Steve across seasons) as elements of the show's creative quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strong recurring comedic devices and character evolution (design/voice/personality adjustments) are cited as contributors to creative longevity and comedic flexibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing-staff continuity and turnover
rubrics_metrics.description: Impact of changes in writing staff on the show (noted that between seasons eight and nine a large percentage of writing staff was new).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stability and experience of writers are treated as factors influencing episode quality and show evolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Network relocation, scheduling, and platform release strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Effects of moving networks (Fox to TBS and back), timeslot shifts, early social-media debuts, and reruns/syndication on presentation and airing (dates, premiere vs linear broadcast differences).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broadcast platform, scheduling, and release strategy influence audience reach and can be evaluated for their impact on a show's success and visibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Home media and regional release availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Home-video release schedules across regions (Region 1/2/4 tables of release dates per season) and need for updated citations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Availability and completeness of home media releases are criteria for accessibility and archival quality for fans and researchers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crossovers and franchise integration
rubrics_metrics.description: Cross-appearance of characters with other animated sitcoms (e.g., Family Guy, Cleveland Show, The Simpsons) and crossover events (Night of the Hurricane).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Degree of integration with other franchises or shared-universe events functions as a creative and promotional metric that can enhance visibility and fan engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awards and nominations as proxy measures of industry recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: Listing of multiple awards and nominations across years and categories (Annie, Artios, ASCAP, GLAAD, Golden Reel, Emmys, Prism, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aggregate awards/nominations across categories and years are used as industry-level indicators of a show's artistic, technical, and cultural merits.
